newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares slip at close, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares slip at close, seen consolidating.

text.p: Singapore shares shifted lower at the close on Friday and dealers said they saw blue chips consolidating possibly for the next two weeks.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index fell 11.58 points to 2,188.09 at the close. Market volume was a moderate 124.61 million shares with declines ahead of advances by 173 to 128.
"The market is drifting down. There is just no kick," said a dealer. He said the December holiday lull had already started but window dressing was still seen to give stocks a late push.
Dealers said active interest in lower-valued stocks would probably be the main feature over the next two weeks.

The market was looking to the debut of infrastucture company Wee Poh on Monday. Wee Poh's initial public offer was 101 times subscribed. The IPO fever in Singapore has fueled premiums of over 50 percent in newly listed shares over their IPO price on their initial days of trading.
Blue chips Singapore Press foreign, Keppel Corp and Fraser & Neave dropped between Singapore $0.50 (US$0.36) and S$0.30 each.

Malaysia's Tan Chong Motor kept its top active spot with over 7.0 million shares but fell S$0.13 to S$2.50 after rallying on its requotation on Thursday. Lower-valued stocks Flextech, Nobel and Singatronics were active.
